title: Exercises on a Pride and Prejudice extract: multiple-choice and true/false questions about Elizabeth and Mr Darcy's argument
summary: Exercises based on a Pride and Prejudice extract: multiple-choice questions about why Elizabeth dislikes Mr Darcy and his proposal, plus true/false statements checking comprehension of key details in their conversation about Mr Wickham.

title: Exercises on a Pride and Prejudice extract: comprehension questions, vocabulary matching, and a writing task
summary: Questions requiring students to explain characters' reactions in the Pride and Prejudice extract, a vocabulary exercise matching six words to their meanings, and a creative writing task asking students to imagine writing a letter from Elizabeth to Mr Wickham.

title: Exercises on a Pride and Prejudice extract: ordering events and answering comprehension questions
summary: A sequencing exercise asking students to arrange five events from a Pride and Prejudice extract in chronological order, followed by six comprehension questions about Mr Darcy's words, Elizabeth's feelings, and Lady Catherine's visit.

title: Vocabulary, sentence completion, and writing tasks based on a Pride and Prejudice extract
summary: A vocabulary exercise finding six words in the text, a sentence completion task using those words, and a writing activity where students imagine being Mr Darcy writing a letter to his aunt about his engagement to Elizabeth Bennet.

title: Exercises on As You Like It extracts: event sequencing, comprehension questions, and character matching
summary: Tasks based on As You Like It extracts including sequencing five events about Orlando and Oliver, answering five questions about their conflict and Rosalind's position at court, and matching five characters with descriptions of who they are.

title: Old English vocabulary comparison and a creative writing task based on As You Like It
summary: A comparison activity asking students to identify modern English equivalents of old English words used in the As You Like It extracts, followed by a writing task imagining what happens next in the upcoming fight between Charles and Orlando.

title: Exercises on As You Like It extracts: multiple-choice and true/false questions about escape and the forest
summary: Multiple-choice questions about Celia and Rosalind's escape and the court's reaction, plus eight true/false statements checking understanding of Hisperia's report, the disguised characters, and Silvius and Corin's conversation about love in the forest.

title: Old English vocabulary, summary completion, and a writing task based on As You Like It extracts
summary: A comparison exercise identifying old English words for modern equivalents, a gap-fill summary of the As You Like It extracts using words from the modern version, and a creative writing task imagining Rosalind and Silvius discussing their broken hearts.
